Standing Desk Buying Guide

A standing desk changes how you work. This guide covers the frame, the desktop, and the accessories that make a height adjustable desk comfortable for a full day, from the floor under your feet to the tray that keeps cords out of sight.

Frame and Motor

A dual motor frame lifts faster and holds more weight than a single motor frame. Check the lifting capacity against the weight of your monitor, laptop, and accessories, and listen to the noise level while the desk moves. We recommend the Uplift V2 and the Fully Jarvis most often, and the Nevi from Herman Miller is the premium pick if budget is not a concern.

Floor Comfort

An anti fatigue mat is the accessory most people skip and later regret. Standing on a hard floor tires your feet within an hour. A good anti fatigue mat cushions your heels and encourages small movements that keep your legs from stiffening. We tested six mats, and the thicker anti fatigue mat models held up best over a month of daily use.

Keeping Cables Tidy

Cable management matters more on a desk that moves. Route power and monitor cables through a tray under the desk so nothing pulls when the desk rises. A tray and a few velcro ties are enough for most setups, and tidy cable management keeps the floor behind the desk clear.

Desktop Size and Materials

Desk surfaces range from 42 inches to 72 inches wide. Bamboo and laminate are the common choices for a standing desk. Laminate resists scratches and costs less, while bamboo looks warmer. Measure your room before you order and leave space behind the desk for the frame to move.

Budget and Warranty

Expect to spend between 300 and 700 dollars for a reliable standing desk with a dual motor frame. A good warranty covers the motor and the frame for at least five years. Herman Miller offers a twelve year warranty, which is part of what you pay for.

Verdict

Pick a stable desk with a dual motor frame, add an anti fatigue mat, and plan your cord routing before the desk arrives. Your posture and your feet will thank you.
